subject: Mental Models
title: Self-Organization
description: A short lesson to help you apply Self-Organization.

hook.text: Starlings form breathtaking murmurations in the sky. No bird leads.

buildup.text: Self-organization occurs when local interactions produce global order without any central controller or blueprint.

discovery.text: Crystals self-organize. So do economies, languages, and Wikipedia.

twist.text: Self-organization does not mean optimal. It means stable. Traffic jams self-organize too.

climax.text: To guide self-organizing systems, change the local rules rather than trying to impose top-down control.

punchline.text: Change the rules each part follows. The order reshapes itself.

quiz.question: How do you guide a self-organizing system?
options: Change the local rules that individual parts follow
Add more parts to the system
